items.description: Kaohsiung is a major port city in southern Taiwan known for its expansive harbor and vibrant urban culture. It serves as an essential economic hub and maritime gateway for the island.

Yuanlin is a bustling city in Changhua County, recognized for its central location and agricultural trade significance. It transitioned from a township to a city in 2015 due to rapid urban development.

Magong is the capital city of the Penghu Islands, located on the main island of the archipelago. It is a historical maritime center known for its well-preserved traditional streets and temple culture.
This grand shrine in Taipei commemorates those who died serving the Republic of China in various conflicts. Its architecture is inspired by the Forbidden City in Beijing.
Located in Banqiao, this complex is the best-preserved example of traditional Taiwanese garden architecture. It reflects the wealth and influence of the Lin family in the Qing dynasty.
This historic fort in Tamsui was established by the Spanish in the 17th century and later controlled by the Dutch. It represents the early colonial period in Taiwan.
These striking industrial ruins in New Taipei City were formerly part of a copper smelting facility in the Shuinandong area. Today, they stand as a prominent landmark overlooking the sea.
Located on Cijin Island in Kaohsiung, this fort was built in the 19th century to guard the entrance to the Kaohsiung harbor. It combines Chinese and Western defensive designs.
Situated at the southernmost point of Taiwan, this fortified lighthouse has guided ships through the dangerous waters of the Bashi Channel since 1883.
Hobe Fort, built in the late 19th century in Tamsui, served as a key defensive installation to protect Taiwan's northern coast from foreign naval attacks.
Located in the mountains of Nantou, this high-altitude farm is famous for its sheep pastures and misty mountain scenery. It is a popular retreat for those seeking fresh air.
This unique mangrove forest tunnel in Tainan is formed by interweaving branches above a waterway. Visitors explore this calm ecosystem by boat.
Xueshan, or Snow Mountain, is the second-highest peak in Taiwan. It is renowned for its glacier-carved cirque and challenging climbing routes.
Qixingshan is the highest dormant volcano in Taiwan, located within Yangmingshan National Park. It features fumaroles and sulfurous vents near the summit.
